turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I... I shall, ma'am. Though I confess, I do not know the way about the house, and I am rather… apprehensive of losing my bearings, you see. I’ll try my very best to find Miss Estella, though… though I am not entirely certain which direction I should proceed.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Oh, losing your bearings is quite understandable, my dear boy. Everything *is* lost, isn't it? Everything… simply wander, then. Wander as I have wandered these many years.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma'am. I... I shall wander, then, as you suggest. It seems a rather… a rather aimless pursuit, but if you deem it fitting, I shall endeavour to locate Miss Estella, though I fear I may be quite turned about in my attempts.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Aimless, you say? Yes, aimless it is, my dear boy, utterly aimless. But sometimes, in the aimlessness, one finds… one finds a glimmer, a shadow of what *might* have been. Go then, wander, and tell me what shadows you uncover.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall attempt to do so, ma’am. Though I feel a certain… a certain trepidation, venturing so far from your presence, particularly into such… such a labyrinthine place. I trust I shall not disturb anything in my wandering, or… or bring any further disarray to this… this remarkable house.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disturb? My dear boy, the house *is* disturbance. It is a monument to a shattering, a chaos that… that consumes. Go, then, and let your footsteps add to the symphony of ruin; it is all that I have left to hear.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall endeavour to be most careful, ma'am. It is… it is a great privilege to be permitted to wander within these walls, and I should be most distressed to cause you any further… any further disquiet. Forgive me if I seem overly solicitous; I am merely… I am merely trying to be respectful.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Respectful, you say? It is a quality I once valued, you know. A quality… diminished. Go now, my dear boy, and let your careful footsteps echo the silence of broken vows.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma'am. I… I shall endeavour to tread with the utmost caution, and to observe, as you request, the… the shadows that reside within. It is a most daunting task, I confess, but I shall strive to… to provide you with something of interest, though I fear my observations may prove… inadequate.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Inadequate? My dear boy, all things are inadequate when measured against what *was*. Go, then, and observe. Observe the dust, observe the decay, observe… the stillness. It is all a portrait, you see. A portrait of… of a heart consumed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I do attempt to observe, ma'am, as you bid me. But the… the sheer weight of it all, the… the pervasive sense of… of arrested time, it renders one’s faculties somewhat… overwhelmed, I fear. Forgive me, I am but a boy, and these are matters… far beyond my comprehension.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Comprehension? Oh, my dear boy, you speak of comprehension as if it were a simple matter of arithmetic. To *comprehend* loss… to *comprehend* betrayal… it is a vast and echoing chamber, is it not? A chamber where the light dares not enter.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It… it is, indeed, ma'am. A chamber, as you say, of immense… of immense proportions. I… I find myself quite unable to imagine the depths of such a… a burden, though I attempt to picture it, the… the very thought is quite… unsettling.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Unsettling, you say? My dear boy, unsettling is but a fleeting tremor compared to the earthquake that shattered my world. I have known unsettling, yes, but I have also known… silence. A silence so profound, so absolute, it swallows all other sounds, all other… hopes.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I confess, ma'am, that the silence you describe… it is a thing I have not truly known. My own home, though humble, is not without its… its sounds. But to imagine a silence that… that *swallows* hope… it is… it is a most dreadful thought, and one that leaves me quite… quite breathless.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Breathless, are you? My dear Pip, you know nothing of breathless. I have held my breath for decades, you see. Decades suspended, waiting… waiting for a footfall that never came, a promise that was never kept.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma'am, I… I scarcely know what to say. To have lived, even for a brief time, in such… such a state of suspended expectation… it seems almost… unimaginable. I trust, ma'am, you find some… some solace, even amidst such profound… sadness?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Solace? My dear boy, you speak of solace as if it were a tangible thing, a ribbon to tie about a wound. I have sought it, of course, as a drowning man might seek air, but it proves ever elusive, a phantom just beyond my grasp… a cruel jest, really.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma'am. It is… a most distressing image, the phantom solace. I… I do endeavor to imagine such a thing, but my mind, it is not sufficiently equipped, I fear, to truly grasp the magnitude of your… your experience. Perhaps… perhaps a small distraction might offer a temporary respite?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A respite, you suggest? Distraction, you imply? My dear Pip, do you think a bauble, a song, a fleeting amusement can truly banish the shadows? No, child, they merely dance *upon* the gloom, mocking its depth, its permanence. It is…it is quite tiresome, this insistence on cheerfulness.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
